reviews.author: Alex Holmes
reviews.summary: Reviews Suno Studio, the browser DAW. The output sounds professional, control is finer than before, and stem and MIDI downloads make it much more useful in a DAW. Results are inconsistent, with some artefacts and a steep learning curve. Stem splitting is hit-and-miss.
reviews.note: MusicTech scored it 6 (out of 10). This covers the v5-era Studio, before v6. The page carries a generic affiliate-commission disclosure.

reviews.author: Janine Heinrichs
reviews.summary: Tested v5.5 on the free and Pro plans. It quickly makes full songs with strong vocals and is good for ideas and demos. Control over melody and structure is limited, and vocals sometimes miss the requested style.
reviews.note: No numeric score, so the rating is our reading of the verdict. The site says it 'may receive compensation' from links to products it reviews. Covers v5.5, which v6 has now replaced.

reviews.author: eesel Team (no individual named)
reviews.summary: First-day look at v6. The writer finds it more controllable and more templated, an improvement for structured pop. Retiring v5.5 is the main pain point. Most of its quality evidence is quoted Reddit reactions (muffled mixes, buried vocals) rather than its own tests.
reviews.note: eesel sells helpdesk AI and has no music product. We found no affiliate links. The page is thin on its own testing, so give it low weight.

reviews.outlet: StraySpark blog: AI Music for Indie Game Soundtracks (Suno, Udio, Stable Audio)
reviews.author: StraySpark
reviews.summary: Calls Suno v5 the most 'musical' of the three and the best for boss themes and cutscenes, though it can slip into an 'AI sound' and repeats over long tracks.
reviews.note: DO NOT SCORE. The article contains clear factual errors: it dates Suno v5 to March 2026 (it shipped in Sept 2025), credits 'Udio Pro v3' with MIDI stems while Udio downloads have been off since Oct 2025, and dates Stable Audio 3 to Dec 2025 (it shipped May 2026). It looks machine-written and unverified.

reviews.outlet: Dubspot blog: Best AI Music Generators in 2026
reviews.author: Theo Nakamura
reviews.summary: Ranks Suno first (8.5) as the best all-rounder for songs with vocals.
reviews.note: DO NOT SCORE. The page says it leans 'on official sources only' (no testing). It has affiliate links.

ratings.note: 168 reviews in the last 12 months; 73% are 1-star and 12% are 5-star. The page shows 1.7 in some places. Mostly billing, credit and support complaints, plus recent complaints that v6 ignores prompts and sounds poor. Suno does not invite reviews.
Under 25 reviews, so don't score. Most are about a year old and praise it as an ideation tool.

strengths: #1 on both Artificial Analysis blind-vote music boards (vocal and instrumental), Oct 2026
Stem and MIDI downloads from Suno Studio (MusicTech)
Strong full songs with vocals, fast (Unite.AI)
weaknesses: Inconsistent results and some audio artefacts (MusicTech)

suno.notes: Strong conflict between the blind-vote benchmark and user sentiment. Artificial Analysis's paid evaluator panel puts v6 first by a clear margin. A MusicTech news piece (https://musictech.com/news/industry/suno-ai-update-v6/, 2026-09-21, Emily Swingle) reports near-unanimous r/SunoAI complaints that v6 sounds flat, muddy and muffled. That piece is secondhand reporting of Reddit, so we didn't score it. Sony and UMG filed a new lawsuit over v6 (reported 2026-09-18). For game devs: commercial use needs a paid plan, and Studio's stems/MIDI are a real plus. Suno makes full tracks, not loops or adaptive layers.

reviews.outlet: Dubspot blog: Best AI Music Generators in 2026
reviews.author: Theo Nakamura
reviews.summary: Ranks Udio fifth (7.0), as a licensed, artist-style music service in a closed environment where creations cannot be exported.
reviews.note: DO NOT SCORE. No testing (official sources only).

Not on the Artificial Analysis music boards
udio.notes: Udio is not usable for game audio right now. Digital Music News (https://www.digitalmusicnews.com/2025/10/31/udio-downloads-disabled-umg-deal/, 2025-10-31, verified) reports that all downloads were switched off without warning. Udio then reopened downloads for 48 hours in early November 2025. Secondary sources say a help-centre note dated 2026-02-17 still lists downloads as disabled, and that the licensed 'walled garden' relaunch planned for 2026 has no confirmed date for restoring downloads (unverified). We found no confirmation that the relaunch has happened. We found no independent hands-on review from the last 18 months. Older reviews (e.g. Tom's Guide by Nigel Powell, probably 2024) cover the pre-settlement product and are stale. Consider delisting Udio from 'audio' or flagging it 'no export'. Check udio.com by hand.

benchmarks.value: On video-to-audio, Sonilo SFX 1.0 beats Mirelo v1.6 on most metrics (e.g. DeSync 0.65 vs 0.67 on Movie Gen Bench; Audiobox PQ 6.58 vs 6.05). On text-to-audio, Mirelo trails ElevenLabs SFX v2 and Sonilo on CLAP.

Sonilo, a competing video-to-SFX product, wins nearly everything and is linked from the page. That looks like a Sonilo-affiliated evaluation, but the page doesn't say so. Not a leaderboard.

vendor_claims.text: Mirelo SFX 2.0 (2026-10-14). In Mirelo's own blind tests (25 crowd raters x 30 videos per pair), raters preferred it over Sony Woosh 81% vs 9%, Kling Foley 63% vs 18%, Sonilo 46% vs 33%, and over the native audio of Veo 3.1 Fast, MiniMax, Seedance and Kling. Keeps dialogue and replaces music. Up to 10 min. Has an API and MCP; Roblox plugin 'coming soon'.

caveats: 1) Benchmarks: the only current independent blind-vote boards are Artificial Analysis AA-Music v1.1 (Vocal: 13 models; Instrumental: 19). They cover Suno, ElevenLabs and Stable Audio only. Udio, AIVA, SOUNDRAW, Mubert, Beatoven and Mirelo are absent. The AA pages are undated; AlphaSignal reported v1.1 on 2026-10-07 with about 37k panel votes. The CMU Music Arena's only published board (Jul-Aug 2025) has no listed commercial service except open Stable Audio, and its live site returned an empty page. We found no independent SFX or video-to-SFX leaderboard. Academic V2A benchmarks didn't name commercial services in their abstracts, and the one comparison with numbers (audio_eval) looks Sonilo-affiliated. 2) Ranks are positions in AA's listed order; AA shows overlapping CI rank ranges, so neighbouring percentiles are not statistically distinct. 3) Open question: which model stableaudio.com runs (2.5 vs 3 Large; the percentile changes from 16.7 to 61.1). For ElevenLabs, whether v1 is still selectable (instrumental 66.7 vs 44.4). 4) Reviews are thin and mostly SEO or affiliate roundups that don't test anything. We excluded those (marked 'DO NOT SCORE'). One StraySpark music article contains clear factual errors and is excluded. MusicTech's Suno Studio review is the strongest independent review found. 5) The WebSearch budget (shared across the session) ran out after about 30 searches, before dedicated searches for Beatoven, Mubert and SOUNDRAW reviews, game-audio forums (VI-Control, KVR, Unity/Godot forums) and YouTube same-input comparisons. Community mentions are therefore 0 for every tool. Reddit/X were skipped by instruction. G2/Capterra were not attempted (usually 403). 6) User ratings are dominated by billing complaints (Suno, Soundraw, Mubert) and Udio's download shutdown; none of the review-site profiles invite reviews. 7) Big picture for game devs: Suno leads the blind-vote quality benchmarks but faces strong v6 user backlash and new label litigation. Udio currently can't export at all.
